title: Analytic Test
text: time evolution size spectrum \(N(w)\) described McKendrick-von Foerster equation added diffusion term: \[\begin{equation}   \frac{\partial N}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial w} \left( g N - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial(D N)}{\partial w} \right) = -\mu N, \end{equation}\] \(g(w)\) growth rate, \(\mu(w)\) mortality rate \(D(w)\) diffusion rate. look solutions rates power laws form: \[\begin{align} g(w) &= w^p, \\ \mu(w) &= B w^{p-1}, \\ D(w) &= K w^{p+1}. \end{align}\]

title: Analytic Test
text: try power-law ansatz solution: \[ N(w) = C w^{-\lambda}. \] Substituting forms transport equation steady state (\(\partial N / \partial t = 0\)): \[ \frac{\partial}{\partial w} \left( w^p C w^{-\lambda} - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial}{\partial w}(K w^{p+1} C w^{-\lambda}) \right) = - B w^{p-1} C w^{-\lambda}. \] simplify term inside derivative: \[ D N = K C w^{p+1-\lambda}, \] \[ \frac{\partial(D N)}{\partial w} = K C (p+1-\lambda) w^{p-\lambda}, \] \[ g N - \frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial(D N)}{\partial w} = \left( - \frac{1}{2} K (p+1-\lambda) \right) C w^{p-\lambda}.\] Thus flux \(J = J_0 w^{p-\lambda}\) \(J_0 = C \left( - \frac{1}{2} K (p+1-\lambda) \right)\). Differentiating flux respect \(w\) gives \[ \frac{\partial J}{\partial w} = J_0 (p-\lambda) w^{p-\lambda-1}. \] RHS \[ -\mu N = - B C w^{p-1-\lambda}. \] Equating LHS RHS gives \[ C \left( - \frac{1}{2} K (p+1-\lambda) \right) (p-\lambda) w^{p-\lambda-1} = - B C w^{p-\lambda-1}. \] Dividing \(C w^{p-\lambda-1}\) (assuming \(C \neq 0\) \(w \neq 0\)): \[ \left( - \frac{1}{2} K (p+1-\lambda) \right) (p-\lambda) + B = 0. \] Let \(x = p - \lambda\). \(p + 1 - \lambda = x + 1\). equation becomes: \[ \left( - \frac{1}{2} K (x+1) \right) x + B = 0. \] , equivalently, \[ Ax - \frac{1}{2} K x^2 - \frac{1}{2} K x + B = 0. \] multiply -2: \[ K x^2 - (2A - K) x - 2B = 0. \] quadratic equation \(x = p - \lambda\). solutions : \[ x = \frac{(2A - K) \pm \sqrt{(2A - K)^2 + 8KB}}{2K}.\] interested solution corresponds limit small diffusion \(K \0\). limit, \(g N \sim C w^{p-\lambda}\) \(\frac{\partial (gN)}{\partial w} \sim C (p-\lambda) w^{p-\lambda-1}\). transport equation without diffusion \(\frac{\partial (gN)}{\partial w} = -\mu N\). \[ (p-\lambda) = -B \implies x = p-\lambda = -B/. \] Since \(, B > 0\), \(x\) negative. Let’s check roots. \((2A-K)^2 + 8KB > (2A-K)^2\), square root larger \(|2A-K|\). term \((2A-K)\) positive small \(K\). positive root \(\frac{(2A-K) + \text{larger}}{2K} > 0\). negative root \(\frac{(2A-K) - \text{larger}}{2K} < 0\). need negative root: \[ \begin{split} \lambda &= p - \frac{(2A - K) - \sqrt{(2A - K)^2 + 8KB}}{2K}\\ &=p + \frac{4B}{(2A - K) + \sqrt{(2A - K)^2 + 8KB}}. \end{split} \] second expression better numerical evaluation avoids subtraction two similarly sized numbers.

title: Analytic Test
text: verify analytical solution considering single species mizer checking project() function keeps system steady state. First set mizer model power law rates: can now project forward time check result stays .
code: library(mizer)  # Parameters p <- 0.7 A <- 1 B <- 0.5 K <- 0.1  # Calculate lambda # coefficients for K x^2 - (2A - K) x - 2B = 0 a_quad <- K b_quad <- -(2*A - K) c_quad <- -2*B  det <- b_quad^2 - 4 * a_quad * c_quad x <- 4 * B / (-b_quad + sqrt(det)) lambda <- p + x  # Set up mizer params # We create a dummy species sp <- data.frame(species = "Test",                  w_max = 1000,                  w_mat = 100) params <- newMultispeciesParams(sp, no_w = 1000, min_w = 1e-3,                                 info_level = 0)  # Set initial N to analytical solution initialN(params) <- matrix(w(params)^(-lambda), nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)  # Define custom rate functions # Growth start_growth <- function(params, ...) {     matrix(A * params@w^p, nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) } params <- setRateFunction(params, "EGrowth", "start_growth")  # Mort start_mort <- function(params, ...) {     matrix(B * params@w^(p - 1), nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) } params <- setRateFunction(params, "Mort", "start_mort")  # Diffusion ext_diffusion(params)[1, ] <- K * w(params)^(p + 1)  # RDD (Constant Flux) params@species_params$constant_reproduction <- getRequiredRDD(params) params <- setRateFunction(params, "RDD", "constantRDD") # Run project # We verify that N stays constant. sim <- project(params, t_max = 1, dt = 0.1, method = "predictor-corrector")  # Compare final N with initial N n0 <- initialN(params)[1, ] n1 <- finalN(sim)[1, ]  # Plot plot(w(params), n0, log="xy", type="l", col="blue", lwd=2,       main="Comparison of numerical and analytical solution",      xlab="Size", ylab="Density") lines(w(params), n1, col="red", lty=2, lwd=2) legend("topright", legend=c("Analytical", "Numerical"),         col=c("blue", "red"), lty=c(1, 2)) # Calculate relative error rel_err <- abs(n1 - n0) / n0 # ignore last 100 bins because they are affected by the right boundary max_rel_err <- max(rel_err[1:980]) print(paste("Maximum relative error:", max_rel_err)) #> [1] "Maximum relative error: 0.00596547751519771"  if (max_rel_err < 0.01) {   print("Test passed: Numerical solution stays close to analytical steady state.") } else {   print("Test failed: Numerical solution deviates from analytical steady state.") } #> [1] "Test passed: Numerical solution stays close to analytical steady state."

title: Analytic Test
text: verify time-dependent solution starting simulation analytical distribution small time \(t_{start} > 0\) (avoid singularity \(t=0\)) projecting later time \(t_{end}\). can simplify left boundary condition far enough away Gaussian us set solution 0 . Now project forward time.  looks good let us also look agreement quantitatively:
code: # Function to calculate N analytic N_analytic <- function(w, t, w0, t0, K_eff = 0.1) {   # Parameters   p <- 0.7   A <- 1   B <- 0.5      # Transformed parameters   U <- A - 0.5 * K_eff   V <- 0.5 * K_eff * (1 - p)   b <- B / (1 - p)   nu <- sqrt((U/V)^2 + 4 * b / V)    # Time elapsed   dt <- t - t0   if (dt <= 0) stop("t must be greater than t0")      # Transform to x   x <- w^(1 - p) / (1 - p)   x0 <- w0^(1 - p) / (1 - p)      # Argument for Bessel   z <- 2 * sqrt(x * x0) / (V * dt)      # Logarithm of N_tilde using scaled Bessel to avoid overflow   bessel_scaled <- besselI(z, nu, expon.scaled = TRUE)      log_N_tilde <- -log(V * dt) +                   (U / (2 * V)) * log(x / x0) -                   (x + x0) / (V * dt) +                   z +                   log(bessel_scaled)      N_tilde <- exp(log_N_tilde)      # Transform back to N(w)   N <- N_tilde * w^(-p)      return(N) } # Initial Condition w0 <- 1e-2 t_start <- 0.1 t_end <- 2  # Set initial N from analytical solution initial_n <- N_analytic(w(params), t_start, w0, 0) initialN(params) <- matrix(initial_n, nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) # Set RDD to 0 params@species_params$constant_reproduction <- 0 params <- setRateFunction(params, "RDD", "constantRDD") # Run project sim <- project(params, t_max = t_end - t_start, dt = 0.05,                t_save = t_end - t_start,                method = "predictor-corrector")  # Compare final_n_num <- finalN(sim)[1, ] final_n_ana <- N_analytic(w(params), t_end, w0, 0)  # Plot plot(w(params), final_n_num, log = "x", type = "l", col = "red", lwd = 2,       main = "Time Dependent Check", xlab = "Size", ylab = "Density")  lines(w(params), final_n_ana, col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2) legend("topright", legend = c("Numerical", "Analytical"),        col = c("red", "blue"), lty = c(1, 2)) # Robust comparison metrics # 1. Total Abundance (Conservation) total_n_num <- sum(final_n_num * params@dw) total_n_ana <- sum(final_n_ana * params@dw) rel_err_total <- abs(total_n_num - total_n_ana) / total_n_ana  # 2. Peak Location peak_idx_num <- which.max(final_n_num) peak_idx_ana <- which.max(final_n_ana) peak_w_num <- w(params)[peak_idx_num] peak_w_ana <- w(params)[peak_idx_ana] rel_err_peak_loc <- abs(peak_w_num - peak_w_ana) / peak_w_ana  # 3. Peak Height peak_val_num <- max(final_n_num) peak_val_ana <- max(final_n_ana) rel_err_peak_val <- abs(peak_val_num - peak_val_ana) / peak_val_ana  print(paste("Total Abundance Error:", rel_err_total)) #> [1] "Total Abundance Error: 0.00480520170128005" print(paste("Peak Location Error:", rel_err_peak_loc)) #> [1] "Peak Location Error: 0.0406391712906862" print(paste("Peak Height Error:", rel_err_peak_val)) #> [1] "Peak Height Error: 0.0323776398076434"  # Pass conditions:  #   < 0.5% abundance error,  #   < 5% location shift,  #   < 4% height difference (diffusive flattening) if (rel_err_total < 0.005 &&      rel_err_peak_loc < 0.05 &&      rel_err_peak_val < 0.04) {   print("Time-dependent test passed.") } else {   print("Time-dependent test failed.") } #> [1] "Time-dependent test passed."

title: Analytic Test
text: Euler method uses first-order upwind treatment advective growth term. introduces numerical diffusion. locally constant growth rate grid spacing, expected numerical diffusion \[ D_\mathrm{num} \approx g(w) \Delta w + g(w)^2 \Delta t. \] logarithmic mizer grid approximately \(\Delta w = (\beta_\mathrm{grid} - 1)w\). keep analytical solution power-law family, use special case \(p = 1\). \(g(w) = w\) numerical diffusion terms scale like \(w^2\): \[ D_\mathrm{num}(w) \approx \left((\beta_\mathrm{grid} - 1) + ^2 \Delta t\right)w^2. \] Euler method physical diffusion \(K w^2\) behave like continuous equation \[ K_\mathrm{eff} = K + (\beta_\mathrm{grid} - 1) + ^2 \Delta t. \] \(p = 1\) transformed variable \(x = \log w\). density \(\tilde N(x, t) = w N(w, t)\) satisfies advection-diffusion equation constant diffusion constant mortality. Green’s function therefore lognormal density: \[ N(w,t) = \frac{\exp[-B(t-t_0)]}{w}   \phi\left(\log w;\,             \log w_0 + \left(- \frac{K_\mathrm{eff}}{2}\right)(t-t_0),             K_\mathrm{eff}(t-t_0)\right), \] \(\phi(x; m, v)\) normal density mean \(m\) variance \(v\). project Euler method compare exact solution effective diffusion coefficient.
code: # Parameters for the Euler numerical diffusion check p_euler <- 1 A_euler <- 1 B_euler <- 0.5 K_euler <- 0.1 dt_euler <- 0.01  N_lognormal <- function(w, t, w0, t0, K_eff) {     dt <- t - t0     if (dt <= 0) stop("t must be greater than t0")          x <- log(w)     mean_x <- log(w0) + (A_euler - 0.5 * K_eff) * dt          exp(-B_euler * dt) *         dnorm(x, mean = mean_x, sd = sqrt(K_eff * dt)) / w }  start_growth_euler <- function(params, ...) {     matrix(A_euler * params@w^p_euler, nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) }  start_mort_euler <- function(params, ...) {     matrix(B_euler * params@w^(p_euler - 1), nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) }  params_euler <- newMultispeciesParams(sp, no_w = 1000, min_w = 1e-3,                                       info_level = 0) params_euler <- setRateFunction(params_euler, "EGrowth",                                 "start_growth_euler") params_euler <- setRateFunction(params_euler, "Mort", "start_mort_euler") ext_diffusion(params_euler)[1, ] <- K_euler * w(params_euler)^2  # The pulse stays well away from the left boundary, so no recruitment enters. params_euler@species_params$constant_reproduction <- 0 params_euler <- setRateFunction(params_euler, "RDD", "constantRDD")  beta_grid <- w(params_euler)[2] / w(params_euler)[1] K_num <- A_euler * (beta_grid - 1) + A_euler^2 * dt_euler K_eff <- K_euler + K_num  w0_euler <- 1e-2 t_start_euler <- 0.1 t_end_euler <- 1  initial_n_euler <- N_lognormal(w(params_euler), t_start_euler, w0_euler,                                0, K_eff) initialN(params_euler) <- matrix(initial_n_euler, nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE) sim_euler <- project(params_euler,                      t_max = t_end_euler - t_start_euler,                      dt = dt_euler,                      t_save = t_end_euler - t_start_euler,                      t_start = t_start_euler,                      method = "euler",                      progress_bar = FALSE)  final_n_euler <- finalN(sim_euler)[1, ] final_n_euler_ana <- N_lognormal(w(params_euler), t_end_euler, w0_euler,                                  0, K_eff)  plot(w(params_euler), final_n_euler, log = "x", type = "l", col = "red",      lwd = 2, main = "Euler Check with Numerical Diffusion",      xlab = "Size", ylab = "Density") lines(w(params_euler), final_n_euler_ana, col = "blue", lty = 2, lwd = 2) legend("topright", legend = c("Euler", "Analytical with K_eff"),        col = c("red", "blue"), lty = c(1, 2)) total_euler <- sum(final_n_euler * params_euler@dw) total_euler_ana <- sum(final_n_euler_ana * params_euler@dw) rel_err_total_euler <- abs(total_euler - total_euler_ana) / total_euler_ana  peak_idx_euler <- which.max(final_n_euler) peak_idx_euler_ana <- which.max(final_n_euler_ana) peak_w_euler <- w(params_euler)[peak_idx_euler] peak_w_euler_ana <- w(params_euler)[peak_idx_euler_ana] rel_err_peak_loc_euler <- abs(peak_w_euler - peak_w_euler_ana) /     peak_w_euler_ana  peak_val_euler <- max(final_n_euler) peak_val_euler_ana <- max(final_n_euler_ana) rel_err_peak_val_euler <- abs(peak_val_euler - peak_val_euler_ana) /     peak_val_euler_ana  print(paste("Expected numerical diffusion coefficient:", K_num)) #> [1] "Expected numerical diffusion coefficient: 0.0239254075588153" print(paste("Effective diffusion coefficient:", K_eff)) #> [1] "Effective diffusion coefficient: 0.123925407558815" print(paste("Total Abundance Error:", rel_err_total_euler)) #> [1] "Total Abundance Error: 0.00112189285798662" print(paste("Peak Location Error:", rel_err_peak_loc_euler)) #> [1] "Peak Location Error: 0" print(paste("Peak Height Error:", rel_err_peak_val_euler)) #> [1] "Peak Height Error: 0.0245757881629701"  if (rel_err_total_euler < 0.005 &&     rel_err_peak_loc_euler < 0.005 &&     rel_err_peak_val_euler < 0.05) {   print("Euler numerical diffusion test passed.") } else {   print("Euler numerical diffusion test failed.") } #> [1] "Euler numerical diffusion test passed."

title: Analytic Test
text: first-order upwind discretisation growth term introduces numerical diffusion even predictor-corrector time step used. method leading-order time discretisation diffusion removed, expected additional diffusion spatial contribution \[D_\mathrm{num}(w) \approx g(w) \Delta w.\] logarithmic mizer grid power-law form physical diffusion: \[ D_\mathrm{num}(w) \approx (\beta_\mathrm{grid} - 1) w^{p+1}. \] can therefore check whether agreement improves exact solution evaluated \[K_\mathrm{eff} = K + (\beta_\mathrm{grid} - 1).\]
code: beta_grid <- w(params)[2] / w(params)[1] K_num_pc <- A * (beta_grid - 1) K_eff_pc <- K + K_num_pc  final_n_ana_pc <- N_analytic(w(params), t_end, w0, 0, K_eff_pc)  total_n_ana_pc <- sum(final_n_ana_pc * params@dw) rel_err_total_pc <- abs(total_n_num - total_n_ana_pc) / total_n_ana_pc  peak_idx_ana_pc <- which.max(final_n_ana_pc) peak_w_ana_pc <- w(params)[peak_idx_ana_pc] rel_err_peak_loc_pc <- abs(peak_w_num - peak_w_ana_pc) / peak_w_ana_pc  peak_val_ana_pc <- max(final_n_ana_pc) rel_err_peak_val_pc <- abs(peak_val_num - peak_val_ana_pc) / peak_val_ana_pc  print(paste("Predictor-corrector numerical diffusion coefficient:", K_num_pc)) #> [1] "Predictor-corrector numerical diffusion coefficient: 0.0139254075588153" print(paste("Predictor-corrector effective diffusion coefficient:", K_eff_pc)) #> [1] "Predictor-corrector effective diffusion coefficient: 0.113925407558815" print(paste("Adjusted Total Abundance Error:", rel_err_total_pc)) #> [1] "Adjusted Total Abundance Error: 0.00066753836710786" print(paste("Adjusted Peak Location Error:", rel_err_peak_loc_pc)) #> [1] "Adjusted Peak Location Error: 0" print(paste("Adjusted Peak Height Error:", rel_err_peak_val_pc)) #> [1] "Adjusted Peak Height Error: 0.0226085133793947"  if (rel_err_total_pc < rel_err_total &&     rel_err_peak_loc_pc <= rel_err_peak_loc &&     rel_err_peak_val_pc < rel_err_peak_val) {   print("Accounting for numerical diffusion improves the agreement.") } else {   print("Accounting for numerical diffusion does not improve all metrics.") } #> [1] "Accounting for numerical diffusion improves the agreement."  # Pass conditions:  #   < 0.5% abundance error,  #   < 5% location shift,  #   < 4% height difference (diffusive flattening) if (rel_err_total_pc < 0.001 &&     rel_err_peak_loc_pc < 1e-6 &&     rel_err_peak_val_pc < 0.03) {   print("Numerical diffusion test passed.") } else {   print("Numerical diffusion test failed.") } #> [1] "Numerical diffusion test passed."

title: Analytic Test
text: project() offers three time-stepping schemes (method argument): first-order "euler" scheme two second-order schemes "predictor_corrector" (Crank-Nicolson corrector) "tr_bdf2" (L-stable TR-BDF2 scheme). time-dependent solution lets us verify orders directly. read temporal order comparison analytic solution, error dominated spatial numerical diffusion first-order upwind scheme (see previous section), independent time step vanish \(\Delta t \0\). isolate temporal error instead measure self-convergence: method compare solution obtained time step \(\Delta t\) reference solution method computed small time step. fixed spatial discretisation error cancels difference, leaving time-discretisation error, whose decay reveals order scheme. project longer horizon , even largest steps probe take several steps, sweep step size two decades, \(\Delta t = 1.6\) \(\Delta t = 0.025\). travelling pulse stays well within grid horizon, error norm, restricted bulk, free boundary effects. fitted slopes confirm expected behaviour: "euler" first order "predictor_corrector" "tr_bdf2" second order.  asymptotic range (small \(\Delta t\)) two second-order curves run parallel slope-2 guide line, four times accurate halving time step, whereas "euler" curve follows slope-1 line. large steps picture diverges sharply: "predictor_corrector" curve bends well slope-2 line \(\Delta t = 1.6\) error exceeds one, Crank-Nicolson corrector overshoots (rings) large steps. L-stable "tr_bdf2" curve instead stays close slope-2 trend remains order magnitude accurate . large-step robustness discussed Numerical details vignette.
code: elapsed <- 12.8            # length of the run (the pulse stays on the grid) dt_ref  <- 0.025 / 8       # reference step, much finer than any tested step dts     <- 1.6 / 2^(0:6)   # tested steps: 1.6, 0.8, ..., 0.025 methods <- c("euler", "predictor_corrector", "tr_bdf2")  wv <- w(params) dwv <- params@dw  run_to_end <- function(method, dt) {     sim <- project(params, t_max = elapsed, dt = dt, t_save = elapsed,                    method = method, progress_bar = FALSE)     finalN(sim)[1, ] }  # Restrict the error norm to the bulk of the travelling pulse, away from the # boundaries. n_ana_end <- N_analytic(wv, t_start + elapsed, w0, 0) mask <- n_ana_end > max(n_ana_end) * 1e-4 rel_L2 <- function(num, ref) {     sqrt(sum((num[mask] - ref[mask])^2 * dwv[mask]) /          sum(ref[mask]^2 * dwv[mask])) }  err <- matrix(NA, length(dts), length(methods),               dimnames = list(NULL, methods)) for (m in methods) {     ref <- run_to_end(m, dt_ref)     for (i in seq_along(dts)) {         err[i, m] <- rel_L2(run_to_end(m, dts[i]), ref)     } }  # Fitted order over the asymptotic range (the coarsest step is outside it). order_of <- function(m) {     keep <- dts <= 0.1     unname(coef(lm(log(err[keep, m]) ~ log(dts[keep])))[2]) } ord <- sapply(methods, order_of) print(round(ord, 2)) #>               euler predictor_corrector             tr_bdf2  #>                0.99                2.01                2.01 cols <- c(euler = "#E69F00", predictor_corrector = "#009E73",           tr_bdf2 = "#0072B2") pchs <- c(euler = 16, predictor_corrector = 17, tr_bdf2 = 15)  plot(NA, xlim = range(dts), ylim = range(err), log = "xy",      xlab = expression(Delta * t),      ylab = "relative L2 self-convergence error",      main = "Temporal order of convergence") for (m in methods) {     lines(dts, err[, m], col = cols[m], pch = pchs[m], type = "b", lwd = 2) }  # Slope-1 and slope-2 guide lines, anchored at the finest step. i0 <- length(dts) lines(dts, err[i0, "euler"]   * (dts / dts[i0])^1, lty = 3, col = "grey50") lines(dts, err[i0, "tr_bdf2"] * (dts / dts[i0])^2, lty = 2, col = "grey50")  legend("bottomright", bty = "n",        legend = c(sprintf("euler (order %.2f)", ord["euler"]),                   sprintf("predictor_corrector (order %.2f)",                           ord["predictor_corrector"]),                   sprintf("tr_bdf2 (order %.2f)", ord["tr_bdf2"]),                   "slope 1", "slope 2"),        col = c(cols, "grey50", "grey50"),        pch = c(pchs, NA, NA), lty = c(1, 1, 1, 3, 2), lwd = 2)

code: build_sp <- function(no_w, second_order) {     sp <- data.frame(species = "Test", w_max = 1000, w_mat = 100,                      n = p, z0 = 0, z_ext = B, d = p - 1, D_ext = K)     pr <- newMultispeciesParams(sp, no_w = no_w, min_w = 1e-3, info_level = 0)     second_order_w(pr) <- second_order     pr <- setRateFunction(pr, "EGrowth", "start_growth")     pr@interaction[] <- 0           # no predation: total mortality is B w^(p-1)     pr <- setExtMort(pr)     pr@species_params$constant_reproduction <- 0     setRateFunction(pr, "RDD", "constantRDD") }  # Cell average (= cell-centre value) for the second-order scheme, node value for # the first-order scheme. ref_w <- function(pr, second_order) {     wv <- w(pr)     if (second_order) wv * sqrt(wv[2] / wv[1]) else wv }  pulse_err <- function(no_w, second_order, dt = 0.0025) {     pr <- build_sp(no_w, second_order)     rw <- ref_w(pr, second_order)     initialN(pr) <- matrix(N_analytic(rw, t_start, w0, 0), nrow = 1)     sim <- project(pr, t_max = t_end - t_start, dt = dt,                    t_save = t_end - t_start, method = "tr_bdf2",                    progress_bar = FALSE)     num <- finalN(sim)[1, ]     ana <- N_analytic(rw, t_end, w0, 0)     mask <- ana > max(ana) * 1e-3        # bulk of the pulse, away from boundaries     sqrt(sum((num[mask] - ana[mask])^2 * pr@dw[mask]) /          sum(ana[mask]^2 * pr@dw[mask])) }  no_ws <- c(50, 100, 200, 400, 800) dx <- log(1000 / 1e-3) / no_ws            # log-size grid spacing err_first  <- sapply(no_ws, pulse_err, second_order = FALSE) err_second <- sapply(no_ws, pulse_err, second_order = TRUE)  sp_order <- function(e) unname(coef(lm(log(e) ~ log(dx)))[2]) round(c(first_order = sp_order(err_first),         second_order = sp_order(err_second)), 2) #>  first_order second_order  #>         0.74         2.04 plot(dx, err_first, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2,      col = "#E69F00", xlab = expression(Delta * x == log * beta),      ylab = "relative L2 error", ylim = range(err_first, err_second),      main = "Spatial order of convergence") lines(dx, err_second, type = "b", pch = 17, lwd = 2, col = "#0072B2")  # slope-1 and slope-2 guide lines, anchored at the finest grid i0 <- length(dx) lines(dx, err_first[i0]  * (dx / dx[i0])^1, lty = 3, col = "grey50") lines(dx, err_second[i0] * (dx / dx[i0])^2, lty = 2, col = "grey50")  legend("bottomright", bty = "n",        legend = c(sprintf("first order (%.2f)", sp_order(err_first)),                   sprintf("second order (%.2f)", sp_order(err_second)),                   "slope 1", "slope 2"),        col = c("#E69F00", "#0072B2", "grey50", "grey50"),        pch = c(16, 17, NA, NA), lty = c(1, 1, 3, 2), lwd = 2) steady_err <- function(no_w, second_order) {     pr <- build_sp(no_w, second_order)     rw <- ref_w(pr, second_order)     initialN(pr) <- matrix(rw^(-lambda), nrow = 1)     pr@species_params$constant_reproduction <- getRequiredRDD(pr)     pr <- setRateFunction(pr, "RDD", "constantRDD")     pr <- steadySingleSpecies(pr, keep = "egg")     num <- initialN(pr)[1, ]     ana <- rw^(-lambda)     no <- length(num)     mask <- seq_len(no) > 0.05 * no & seq_len(no) < 0.85 * no     sqrt(sum((num[mask] - ana[mask])^2 * pr@dw[mask]) /          sum(ana[mask]^2 * pr@dw[mask])) }  err_ss_first  <- sapply(no_ws, steady_err, second_order = FALSE) err_ss_second <- sapply(no_ws, steady_err, second_order = TRUE) round(c(first_order = sp_order(err_ss_first),         second_order = sp_order(err_ss_second)), 2) #>  first_order second_order  #>         0.95         1.35

title: Calculation of Default Parameter Values
text: Calculating default physiological parameters follows sequential dependency chain. One parameter value determines next, starting basic size parameters ending standard metabolic rates: Age maturity (\(\text{age}_{\text{mat}}\)) either supplied directly, derived von Bertalanffy parameters via age_mat_vB(). Maximum intake rate (\(h\)) calculated \(\text{age}_{\text{mat}}\), egg size \(w_{\text{min}}\), maturity size \(w_{\text{mat}}\), assimilation parameters. Search volume (\(\gamma\)) metabolism (\(k_s\)) computed using calculated value \(h\). chain runs ways, changing one parameter rarely changes one thing: giving age_mat makes h depend f0, fc w_mat, h carries change gamma ks. behavioural consequences — particular raising h change feeding level — described “Chained derivations cancellation trap” guide changing model parameters.

title: Calculation of Default Parameter Values
text: maximum intake rate coefficient \(h_i\) species \(\) calculated get_h_default(). derivation based idea average individual must grow egg size \(w_{\text{min}}\) maturity size \(w_{\text{mat}}\) given time \(\text{age}_{\text{mat}}\) feeding constant feeding level \(f_0\) (defaults \(0.6\)). definition, rate somatic growth : \[\frac{dw}{dt} = g(w)\] Prior maturation, individuals invest nothing reproduction (\(\psi(w) = 0\)), growth equal energy available growth reproduction \(E_r(w)\): \[g(w) = \max(0, \alpha f(w) h w^n - \text{metab}(w))\] default assumptions: * feeding level constant: \(f(w) = f_0\). * activity cost zero: \(k = 0\), \(\text{metab}(w) = k_s w^p\). * metabolic exponent equals intake exponent: \(p = n\). Substituting gives: \[\frac{dw}{dt} = \alpha f_0 h w^n - k_s w^n = (\alpha f_0 h - k_s) w^n\] also define critical feeding level \(f_c\) feeding level assimilation exactly balances metabolic costs, .e., \(g(w) = 0\). implies: \[\alpha f_c h w^n = k_s w^n \implies k_s = \alpha f_c h\] Using expression \(k_s\) growth equation yields: \[\frac{dw}{dt} = (\alpha f_0 h - \alpha f_c h) w^n = \alpha h (f_0 - f_c) w^n\] can solve differential equation separating variables integrating birth (\(t = 0\), \(w = w_{\text{min}}\)) maturity (\(t = \text{age}_{\text{mat}}\), \(w = w_{\text{mat}}\)): \[\int_{w_{\text{min}}}^{w_{\text{mat}}} w^{-n} \, dw = \alpha h (f_0 - f_c) \int_{0}^{\text{age}_{\text{mat}}} dt\] Evaluating integrals: \[\frac{w_{\text{mat}}^{1-n} - w_{\text{min}}^{1-n}}{1-n} = \alpha h (f_0 - f_c) \text{age}_{\text{mat}}\] Solving \(h\) gives formula implemented get_h_default(): \[h = \frac{w_{\text{mat}}^{1-n} - w_{\text{min}}^{1-n}}{\text{age}_{\text{mat}} (1-n) \alpha (f_0 - f_c)}\] age maturity known, mizer attempts estimate von Bertalanffy parameters using: \[\text{age}_{\text{mat}} = - \frac{\ln\left(1 - \left(\frac{w_{\text{mat}}}{w_{\infty}}\right)^{1/b}\right)}{k_{\text{vb}}} + t_0\] growth information provided , mizer defaults \(h = 30\). search volume coefficient \(\gamma_i\) calculated get_gamma_default(). selected prey abundance described power-law resource spectrum: \[N_R(w_p) = \kappa w_p^{-\lambda}\] resulting encounter rate lead target feeding level \(f_0\) (default \(0.6\)). encounter rate \(E_i(w)\) predator species \(\) size \(w\) : \[E_i(w) = \gamma_i w^q \int \theta_{iR} N_R(w_p) \phi_i(w, w_p) w_p \, dw_p\] Substituting power-law resource spectrum: \[E_i(w) = \gamma_i w^q \theta_{iR} \kappa \int w_p^{1-\lambda} \phi_i(w, w_p) \, dw_p\] predation kernel depends predator/prey mass ratio \(x = w/w_p\), can substitute \(w_p = w/x\) \(dw_p = -w/x^2 \, dx\): \[\int w_p^{1-\lambda} \phi_i(w/w_p) \, dw_p = w^{2-\lambda} \int_0^\infty x^{\lambda - 2} \phi_i(x) \, dx\] Thus, encounter rate scales size : \[E_i(w) = \gamma_i w^{q + 2 - \lambda} \theta_{iR} \kappa \int_0^\infty x^{\lambda - 2} \phi_i(x) \, dx\] Let us define size-independent component encounter rate : \[A_{\text{avail}, } = \theta_{iR} \kappa \int_0^\infty x^{\lambda - 2} \phi_i(x) \, dx\] \(E_i(w) = \gamma_i w^{q + 2 - \lambda} A_{\text{avail}, }\). feeding level given : \[f_i(w) = \frac{E_i(w)}{E_i(w) + h_i w^n}\] feeding level independent size equal \(f_0\), must require size scaling exponents encounter maximum intake match: \[q + 2 - \lambda = n \implies q = n + \lambda - 2\] holds, size \(w\) cancels : \[f_0 = \frac{\gamma_i A_{\text{avail}, }}{\gamma_i A_{\text{avail}, } + h_i}\] Solving equation \(\gamma_i\) yields: \[\gamma_i = \frac{h_i}{A_{\text{avail}, }} \frac{f_0}{1 - f_0}\] code, \(A_{\text{avail}, }\) calculated numerically setting \(\gamma_i = 1\) evaluating encounter rate maximum size grid point divided appropriate power \(w\): \[\text{avail_energy}_i = \frac{E_{}|_{\gamma_i=1}(w_{\text{max}})}{w_{\text{max}}^{q + 2 - \lambda}}\] , default \(\gamma\) : \[\gamma_i = \frac{h_i}{\text{avail_energy}_i} \frac{f_0}{1 - f_0}\] standard metabolic rate coefficient \(k_{s,}\) calculated get_ks_default(). chosen critical feeding level \(f_c\) (default \(0.2\)) exactly feeding level required assimilation balance metabolism maturity size \(w_{\text{mat}}\). critical feeding level \(f_c\), assimilation rate equals metabolic losses. size \(w_{\text{mat}}\): \[\alpha_i f_c h_i w_{\text{mat}}^n = \text{metab}_i(w_{\text{mat}})\] Using default metabolic cost equation \(\text{metab}_i(w) = k_{s,} w^p\) (activity \(k = 0\)): \[\alpha_i f_c h_i w_{\text{mat}}^n = k_{s,} w_{\text{mat}}^p\] Solving \(k_{s,}\) gives formula: \[k_{s,} = f_c \alpha_i h_i w_{\text{mat}}^{n - p}\] \(n = p\), simplifies : \[k_{s,} = f_c \alpha_i h_i\] models search volume coefficient \(\gamma_i\) provided user target feeding level \(f_0\) , get_f0_default() calculates inverse search volume default. Using relationship derived : \[f_{0,} = \frac{\gamma_i A_{\text{avail}, }}{\gamma_i A_{\text{avail}, } + h_i}\] Since encounter rate calculated given \(\gamma_i\) \(E_i(w) = \gamma_i w^{q+2-\lambda} A_{\text{avail}, }\), evaluate: \[\text{avail_energy}_i = \frac{E_i(w_{\text{max}})}{w_{\text{max}}^{q+2-\lambda}}\] calculate: \[f_{0,} = \frac{1}{h_i / \text{avail_energy}_i + 1}\]

code: ssb_of <- function(params, n, species) {     initialN(params) <- n     getSSB(params)[[species]] }  # The hard rule: the fishery is either fully open or fully shut. hardHCR <- function(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t, effort, ...) {     op <- other_params(params)     if (ssb_of(params, n, op$stock) < op$b_lim) {         effort[op$gear] <- 0     }     mizerFMort(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t = t, effort = effort, ...) }  # The ramped rule: effort increases linearly from zero at B_lim to full at # B_trigger. This is the shape of an ICES "hockey stick" rule. rampHCR <- function(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t, effort, ...) {     op <- other_params(params)     ssb <- ssb_of(params, n, op$stock)     frac <- (ssb - op$b_lim) / (op$b_trigger - op$b_lim)     effort[op$gear] <- effort[op$gear] * min(1, max(0, frac))     mizerFMort(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t = t, effort = effort, ...) } params <- NS_params initial_effort(params)["Otter"] <- 1.5 ssb0 <- getSSB(params)[["Cod"]]  other_params(params)$stock     <- "Cod" other_params(params)$gear      <- "Otter" other_params(params)$b_lim     <- 0.5 * ssb0 other_params(params)$b_trigger <- 0.7 * ssb0  params_hard <- setRateFunction(params, "FMort", "hardHCR") params_ramp <- setRateFunction(params, "FMort", "rampHCR") ssb_series <- function(p, dt, t_max = 30, method = "tr_bdf2") {     sim <- project(p, dt = dt, t_max = t_max, t_save = dt, method = method,                    progress_bar = FALSE)     ssb <- getSSB(sim)[, "Cod"]     data.frame(t = as.numeric(names(ssb)), ssb = ssb / ssb0) }  hard_coarse <- ssb_series(params_hard, dt = 0.1) hard_fine   <- ssb_series(params_hard, dt = 0.0125) ramp_coarse <- ssb_series(params_ramp, dt = 0.1) ramp_fine   <- ssb_series(params_ramp, dt = 0.0125) par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))  plot(ssb ~ t, data = hard_coarse, type = "l", col = 2, ylim = c(0.45, 1.02),      xlab = "time (years)", ylab = expression(SSB / SSB[0]),      main = "Hard switch") lines(ssb ~ t, data = hard_fine, col = 4) abline(h = 0.5, lty = 3) legend("topright", c("dt = 0.1", "dt = 0.0125", expression(B[lim])),        col = c(2, 4, 1), lty = c(1, 1, 3), bty = "n", cex = 0.8)  plot(ssb ~ t, data = ramp_coarse, type = "l", col = 2, ylim = c(0.45, 1.02),      xlab = "time (years)", ylab = expression(SSB / SSB[0]),      main = "Ramped rule") lines(ssb ~ t, data = ramp_fine, col = 4) abline(h = 0.5, lty = 3) legend("topright", c("dt = 0.1", "dt = 0.0125"),        col = c(2, 4), lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.8) par(mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) late <- function(d) d[d$t > 27, ] plot(ssb ~ t, data = late(hard_coarse), type = "l", col = 2,      xlab = "time (years)", ylab = expression(SSB / SSB[0]),      main = "Hard switch, final years") lines(ssb ~ t, data = late(hard_fine), col = 4) abline(h = 0.5, lty = 3) legend("topright", c("dt = 0.1", "dt = 0.0125"),        col = c(2, 4), lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.8) tally <- new.env()  tallyHCR <- function(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t, effort, ...) {     op <- other_params(params)     closed <- ssb_of(params, n, op$stock) < op$b_lim     tally$decisions <- c(tally$decisions, closed)     if (closed) effort[op$gear] <- 0     mizerFMort(params, n, n_pp, n_other, t = t, effort = effort, ...) } params_tally <- setRateFunction(params, "FMort", "tallyHCR")  switching <- function(dt, t_max = 30) {     tally$decisions <- logical(0)     project(params_tally, dt = dt, t_max = t_max, t_save = t_max,             method = "tr_bdf2", progress_bar = FALSE)     # Discard the first half of the decisions as transient     d <- tail(tally$decisions, length(tally$decisions) %/% 2)     c(closed_fraction   = mean(d),       switches_per_year = sum(diff(d) != 0) / code: params <- setComponent(     params, "detritus",     initial_value    = 1e5,     dynamics_fun     = "detritus_dynamics",     encounter_fun    = "detritus_encounter",  # optional     component_params = list(rho = 0.1) ) detritusEncounter <- function(params, n, n_pp, n_other, component, ...) {     params2 <- params     # Drop this component before delegating, or mizerEncounter() calls back     # into this function and recurses.     params2@other_encounter[[component]] <- NULL     mizerEncounter(params2, n = n, n_pp = n_other[[component]],                    n_other = n_other, ...) }  detritusDynamics <- function(params, n_other, rates, dt, component, ...) {     detritus <- n_other[[component]]     p <- params@other_params[[component]]     interaction <- params@species_params$interaction_resource     mort <- as.vector(interaction %*% rates$pred_rate)     target <- p$rate * p$capacity / (p$rate + mort)     # Exact over the step, so the result does not depend on dt     target - (target - detritus) * exp(-(p$rate + mort) * dt) }

title: Guide: Understanding size-spectrum dynamics
text: equations behind reasoning , need exact form. Dynamics — McKendrick–von Foerster equation: “− − deaths” balance , written continuity equation size. \[\frac{\partial N_i(w,t)}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial J_i(w,t)}{\partial w} = -\mu_i(w,t) N_i(w,t)\] derivative \(\partial J_i/\partial w\) net loss growth: flux top bracket minus flux bottom. right-hand side loss death. Growth flux \(J_i = g_i N_i\), boundary condition \(J_i(w_{\min}, t) = R_i(t)\) egg size, \(g_i\) \(\text{g}\cdot\text{year}^{-1}\) \(\mu_i\) \(\text{year}^{-1}\). growth diffusion switched (D_ext > 0, default) flux gains term \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\,\partial(D_i N_i)/\partial w\), smooths sharp peaks spreads cohorts. two integrals predation rate. Encountered food — integrate prey size \(w_p\), weighting mass \(w_p\) gained: \[E_i(w) = \gamma_i(w) \int \Big(\theta_{ip} N_R(w_p) + \sum_j \theta_{ij} N_j(w_p)\Big)\, \phi_i(w/w_p)\, w_p\, dw_p\] Predation mortality — integrate thing predator size \(w'\), counting deaths rather mass: \[\mu_{p,}(w) = \sum_j \int \theta_{ji}\,\big(1 - f_j(w')\big)\,\gamma_j (w')^q\,\phi_j(w'/w)\,N_j(w')\,dw'\] shared factors \(\gamma\), \(\phi\) \(\theta\) makes two sides one coin. \((1 - f_j)\) factor worth noting: satiated predators kill less, species whose predators near \(f = 1\) experiences less mortality abundance alone suggests. applies growth side — realised intake \(f_i h_i w^n = (1 - f_i) E_i\). \(f_i\) approaches 1, intake approaches maximum \(h_i w^n\); approach zero. Feeding level encountered food \(E_i\) maximum intake \(h_i w^n\): \[f_i(w) = \frac{E_i(w)}{E_i(w) + h_i w^n}\] Net energy assimilation (\(\alpha\)) metabolism (\(k_s w^p\), plus activity term \(k w\) defaults zero): \[E_{\text{net},}(w) = \max\big(0,\; \alpha_i f_i(w) h_i w^n - k_{s,} w^p - k_i w\big)\] Growth, reproductive allocation \(\psi_i(w)\): \[g_i(w) = \big(1 - \psi_i(w)\big) E_{\text{net},}(w)\] Predation kernel (lognormal, default), mass ratio \(\text{ppmr} = w/w_p \ge 1\) zero : \[\phi_i(\text{ppmr}) = \exp\!\left[\frac{-\big(\ln(\text{ppmr}/\beta_i)\big)^2}{2\sigma_i^2}\right]\] Resource dynamics — default semichemostat, applied size independently (transport along size axis): \[\frac{\partial N_R(w,t)}{\partial t} = r_R(w)\big[c_R(w) - N_R(w,t)\big] - \mu_R(w,t) N_R(w,t)\] replenishment rate \(r_R(w) = r_{pp} w^{n-1}\), capacity \(c_R(w) = \kappa w^{-\lambda}\) w_pp_cutoff zero , \(\mu_R\) consumption fish. steady state \(N_R = r_R c_R/(r_R + \mu_R)\), .e. resource level \(L = N_R/c_R = r_R/(r_R + \mu_R)\). resource_logistic() replaces bracket \(N_R(1 - N_R/c_R)\) resource_constant() holds \(N_R\) fixed. Egg production Beverton–Holt density dependence: \[R_{p,} = \frac{\epsilon_i}{2 w_{\min}} \int \psi_i(w)\, E_{\text{net},}(w)\, N_i(w)\, dw, \qquad R_i = \frac{R_{\max,} R_{p,}}{R_{\max,} + R_{p,}}\] Defaults worth remembering: beta 30, sigma 2, lambda 2.05, w_pp_cutoff 10 g, kappa 1e11, r_pp 10, resource_dynamics "resource_semichemostat", alpha 0.6, f0 0.6, n 2/3, p 0.7, q \(= \lambda - 2 + n\), erepro 1, R_max \(\infty\), w_min 0.001 g, w_mat \(= w_{\inf}/4\), z0 \(= 0.6\,w_{\inf}^{\,n-1}\). complete mathematical formulation see model description article.

code: sim1 <- project(params, t_max = 10, t_save = 0.2, effort = 2) sim2 <- project(params, t_max = 10, t_save = 0.2, effort = 4) yield1 <- melt(getYield(sim1)) yield2 <- melt(getYield(sim2)) ggplot(yield1) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = sp)) yield1 <- filter(yield1, sp %in% c("Saithe", "Cod", "Haddock", "N.pout")) yield2 <- filter(yield2, sp %in% c("Saithe", "Cod", "Haddock", "N.pout")) p1 <- ggplot(yield1) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = sp)) p1 p2 <- ggplot(yield2) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = sp)) p2 yield1$effort <- as.factor(2) yield2$effort <- as.factor(4) yield <- rbind(yield1, yield2) ggplot(yield) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value,                    colour = sp)) +     facet_grid(cols = vars(effort)) ggplot(yield) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value,                    colour = sp,                   linetype = effort)) p1 <- ggplot(yield1) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = sp)) +     ylim(0,1.75e12) p2 <- ggplot(yield2) +     geom_line(aes(x = time, y = value, colour = sp)) +     ylim(0,1.75e12) # Save plots to temporary files tmp1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") tmp2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") ggsave(tmp1, p1, width = 6, height = 4) ggsave(tmp2, p2, width = 6, height = 4)  # Create visual diff diffviewer::visual_diff(tmp1, tmp2) subplot(p1, p2, shareX = TRUE, shareY = TRUE) plot_ly(yield) %>%      add_lines(x = ~time, y = ~value,                color = ~sp, linetype = ~effort)

However, new models built defaults may differ 3.0.0. build models scratch, check w_inf, w_max w_repro_max mean intend. getTrophicLevel() getTrophicLevelBySpecies() now assign resource size-dependent trophic level, \(T_R(w) = \max(1,\, 1 + \log(w / w_R) / \log(\beta_R))\), instead treating resource trophic level 0. new w_R beta_R arguments control . Trophic levels computed functions therefore higher . Set arguments explicitly need reproduce old numbers. Several fixes correct earlier behaviour change output: summary() MizerSim now reports fishing effort used simulation, rather model’s initial_effort. Gears whose effort varied time show mean, flagged note giving range. printed summary therefore differs simulations run time-varying effort. Now plotDiet() MizerSim accepts time_range argument. diet now computed simulated abundances requested times, defaulting final saved step, rather initial one (#357). components t_save. project() advancing abundances components (set via setComponent()) per saved time step instead per dt step. now integrated dt consumer resource spectra, results models components longer depend t_save. Time-varying effort getRDI(), getRDD(), getFlux(). Convergence behaviour can therefore differ edge cases. use project() method = "predictor_corrector" (new method = "tr_bdf2"), resource components now advanced midpoint rates rather start--step value, reach second-order accuracy time consumer spectra. Results methods therefore differ slightly 3.0. default method = "euler" steady states unchanged. 3.1 adds optional, experimental second-order-accurate finite-volume scheme size variable, controlled new second_order_w slot. default, default results byte-identical 3.0. switch (via second_order_w()<- second_order_w argument new...Params() constructors), size-integrated diagnostics resource spectrum shift \(O(\Delta w)\), calibrated model may need recalibrating. Use unclass(), compare .equal() values, need ignore class. objects also carry print(), summary(), plot() .data.frame() methods, printing looks different bare matrix. setInitialValues() deprecated. Replace , averaging time range, getParams(sim, time_range, geometric_mean). reflects shift interpretation: MizerParams object now represents just model specification also current state (abundances), can extracted simulation getParams(), finalParams() initialParams(). Growth now forced non-negative, preventing unphysical shrinkage. model energy available growth used go negative (example strongly food-limited large individual), growth now clamped zero instead, projected size spectra can differ 2.5.4. warning issued growth stops maturity size. Inherited dt method. project() called existing MizerSim object, dt method now default values stored simulation’s new sim_params slot. pass values differ stored ones, warning issued. use different settings deliberately, pass explicitly expect warning. t_max / t_save effort array. arguments now respected even effort array supplied (#231). t_max simulation extends beyond times effort array using last known effort; t_save save frequency controlled independently, interpolating effort needed. Simulations previously derived length save times solely effort array may now produce different set saved steps. State t_max always saved. project() now warns t_max multiple t_save ensures state t_max saved even final interval shorter t_save (#341). returned simulation may therefore contain one extra saved time step compared 3.0. plot() summary() methods MizerParams, MizerSim mizer array classes now registered S3 methods rather S4 methods, plot() summary() stay plain S3 generics mizer loaded. avoids interfering S4 dispatch packages, code relied plot/summary S4 generics (example via selectMethod() getMethod()) needs adjusting. getMeanMaxWeight() now applies species selector denominator well, values change subset species selected. plotSpectra() axis limits. longer forces y-axis lower limit 1e-20 (auto-scales data) , resource = FALSE, uses min(params@w) rather min(params@w) / 100 default lower size limit. title: Bin-average the weight of a size-spectrum integral — bin_average_weight
text: integral \(\int N(w) K(w)\, dw\) discretised mizer's finite-volume grid \(\sum_j N_j \bar K_j \Delta w_j\), \(N_j\) cell average density bin \([w_j, w_{j+1}]\). weight approximated: \(N_j\) already cell average \(\Delta w_j\) exact, neither abundance bin widths ever passed function. Whether point weight \(K(w_j)\) replaced bin average $$\bar K_j = \frac{1}{\Delta w_j}\int_{w_j}^{w_{j+1}} K(w)\,dw   \approx \tfrac12\big(K(w_j) + K(w_{j+1})\big)$$ controlled bin_average entry model's second_order_w() slot. FALSE (default) K returned unchanged, indicator written function reproduces left-edge Riemann sums previous mizer versions byte--byte. TRUE trapezoidal bin average returned, uniformly second order exact whenever \(K\) linear \(w\) (e.g. first moment \(K = w\), equals \((w_{j+1}^2 - w_j^2)/(2\Delta w_j)\)). gating happens inside, always call rather averaging unconditionally: hard-coded bin average silently changes results models default scheme. K product several size-dependent factors, average product individual factors — average product product averages. Spawning stock biomass, example, averages maturity * w single weight. top bin right-hand neighbour grid, weight left unaveraged (one-sided); density negligible, affect second-order accuracy totals.

text: usually call function directly. Instead, set sel_func column gear_params() "double_sigmoid_length" provide l25, l50, l50_right l25_right values additional columns. setFishing() call function automatically calculating selectivity array. selectivity obtained product two sigmoidal curves, one rising one dropping. sigmoidal rise based two parameters l25 l50 determine length 25% 50% stock selected respectively. sigmoidal drop-based two parameters l50_right l25_right determine length selectivity curve dropped back 50% 25% respectively. selectivity given function $$S(l) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\log(3)\frac{l50 -l}{l50 - l25}\right)}\frac{1}{1 + \exp\left(\log(3)\frac{l50_{right} -l}{l50_{right} - l25_{right}}\right)}$$ size-based model weight based, selectivity function length based, uses length-weight parameters b convert length weight. $$l = \left(\frac{w}{}\right)^{1/b}$$

title: Gaussian-mixture predation kernel — gaussian_mixture_pred_kernel
text: Writing predator mass \(w\), prey mass \(w_p\), \(x = \ln(w / w_p)\), feeding kernel $$ \phi_i(w, w_p) = \sum_j a_{ij} \exp\left[-\frac{(x - \mu_{ij})^2}{2\sigma_{ij}^2}\right], \qquad a_{ij} = \frac{p_{ij}/\sigma_{ij}} {\sum_k p_{ik}/\sigma_{ik}}. $$ predator/prey mass ratios greater equal one, zero smaller ratios. proportional Gaussian-mixture probability density mixing proportions \(p_{ij}\), means \(\mu_{ij}\), standard deviations \(\sigma_{ij}\). scaling makes sum component peak heights equal one. Consequently kernel one, one-component mixture identical lognormal_pred_kernel() beta = exp(kernel_mean) sigma = kernel_sd. three component parameters vectors equal length. function selected species parameter data frame, held list-columns kernel_p, kernel_mean, kernel_sd. values kernel_p must non-negative least one positive value, need sum one normalised function.

title: Construct a MizerSim of the leading oscillatory mode — getOscillationModeSim
text: x MizerParams object steady state, typically output findSteadyState(), list returned getStability(). amplitude Largest relative swing species biomass across cycle, \(\max_i \max_t |B_i(t) - B_i^\ast| / B_i^\ast\).  Default 0.1, meaning strongly oscillating species departs 10 % steady biomass. t_save time interval saved time steps returned MizerSim.  Defaults 0.1. final interval shorter t_save divide period, cycle closes. ... Additional arguments forwarded getStability() x MizerParams object.

title: Construct a MizerSim of the leading oscillatory mode — getOscillationModeSim

title: Construct a MizerSim of the leading oscillatory mode — getOscillationModeSim
text: object shows shape mode — species swing, far, phase relative resource. Whether model actually settles onto oscillation separate question, answered real part eigenvalue: limit cycle real part zero, Hopf bifurcation.

title: mizer: Multi-species size-based modelling in R — mizer-package
text: Using mizer relatively simple.  three main stages: Setting model parameters. done creating object class MizerParams. includes model parameters life history parameters species, range size spectrum. several setup functions help create MizerParams objects particular types models: newSingleSpeciesParams() newCommunityParams() newTraitParams() newMultispeciesParams() Running simulation. done calling project() function model parameters. produces object MizerSim contains results simulation. Exploring results. simulation run, results can explored using range plotting_functions, summary_functions indicator_functions. title: Get encounter rate during projection — mizerEncounter
text: encounter rate \(E_i(w)\) predator species \(\) weight \(w\) encounters food contributions encounter fish prey resource. determined summing prey species resource spectrum integrating prey sizes \(w_p\), weighted predation kernel \(\phi(w,w_p)\): $$ E_i(w) = \gamma_i(w) \int \left( \theta_{ip} N_R(w_p) + \sum_{j} \theta_{ij} N_j(w_p) \right) \phi_i(w,w_p) w_p \, dw_p. $$ \(N_j(w)\) abundance density species \(j\) \(N_R(w)\) abundance density resource. overall prefactor \(\gamma_i(w)\) determines predation power predator. interpreted search volume set setSearchVolume() function. predation kernel \(\phi(w,w_p)\) set setPredKernel() function. species interaction matrix \(\theta_{ij}\) set setInteraction() resource interaction vector \(\theta_{ip}\) taken interaction_resource column params@species_params.

code: # create an example params <- NS_params # In this model each species is caught by a single gear, so there is one # row in the gear parameters for each species, in the same order. # Species without an observation get NA. gear_params(params)$yield_observed <-     c(NA, NA, NA, 3e11, 4e9, 4e10, 5e10, NA, 2e11, 6e10, 3e11, NA)  # Plot with default options plotYieldObservedVsModel(params) #> The following species are not being fished in your model and will not be included in the plot: Sprat, Sandeel, N.pout.   # Plot including also species without observations plotYieldObservedVsModel(params, show_unobserved = TRUE) #> The following species are not being fished in your model and will not be included in the plot: Sprat, Sandeel, N.pout.   # Show the ratio instead plotYieldObservedVsModel(params, ratio = TRUE) #> The following species are not being fished in your model and will not be included in the plot: Sprat, Sandeel, N.pout.   # If several gears catch the same species, their yields are added up. # Give Cod a second gear that takes a quarter of the observed yield. gp <- gear_params(params) gp["Cod, Otter", "yield_observed"] <- 3e11 * 0.75 extra <- gp["Cod, Otter", ] extra$gear <- "Gillnet" extra$yield_observed <- 3e11 * 0.25 gear_params(params) <- rbind(gp, extra)  # Compare only the catch of the Otter gear against its observation plotYieldObservedVsModel(params, gear = "Otter") #> The following species are not being caught by the selected gear and will not be included in the plot: Sprat, Sandeel, N.pout, Herring, Dab, Sole, Plaice.

code: params <- newMultispeciesParams(NS_species_params) #> ℹ No h provided for some species, so using age at maturity to calculate it. #> ℹ Because you have n != p, the default value for `h` is not very good. #> ℹ Because the age at maturity is not known, I need to fall back to using #> von Bertalanffy parameters, where available. #> ℹ Using z0 = z0pre * w_inf ^ z0exp for calculated z0 values. #> ℹ Using f0, h, lambda, kappa and the predation kernel to calculate gamma.  #### Setting allometric encounter rate #######################  # Set coefficient for each species. Here we choose 0.1 for each species encounter_pre <- rep(0.1, nrow(species_params(params)))  # Multiply by power of size with exponent, here chosen to be 3/4 # The outer() function makes it an array species x size allo_encounter <- outer(encounter_pre, w(params)^(3/4))  # Change the external encounter rate in the params object ext_encounter(params) <- allo_encounter

what: Avoid rates that jump as a function of abundance
title: Set own rate function to replace mizer rate function — setRateFunction
text: Make sure rate function depends continuously abundances n, n_pp n_other. tempting write rate switches abruptly state model — fishery closes stock falls limit reference point, predator switches diet preferred prey becomes scarce, mortality kicks critical condition. rate breaks assumption underlying every one mizer's time-stepping methods, freeze rates density update see threshold crossed within step. symptoms quiet: mizer issues warning, trajectory keeps changing refine dt, Newton solver stalls, getStability() reports confident meaningless answer. Choosing L-stable method = "tr_bdf2" project() help, difficulty lies frozen rates rather linear solve. remedy give switch finite width, using linear ramp two thresholds logistic transition, usually realistic model anyway. Rates built max() min() continuous differentiable; much less troublesome, costing accuracy correctness. See Discontinuous rate functions article full story, diagnostics fix.

title: Trapezoidal bin-average of a per-bin weight — trapezoidal_bin_average
text: Internal helper second-order summary integrals. summary diagnostic \(\int N(w) K(w)\, dw\) discretised finite-volume grid \(\sum_j N_j \bar K_j \Delta w_j\), \(N_j\) cell average density bin \([w_j, w_{j+1}]\). second order bin width point weight \(K(w_j)\) must replaced bin average $$\bar K_j = \frac{1}{\Delta w_j}\int_{w_j}^{w_{j+1}} K(w)\,dw   \approx \tfrac12\big(K(w_j) + K(w_{j+1})\big).$$ trapezoidal average \(\tfrac12(K_j + K_{j+1})\) uniformly second order exact whenever \(K\) linear \(w\) (e.g. first moment \(K = w\), equals \((w_{j+1}^2 - w_j^2)/(2\Delta w_j)\)).

title: Collect and report the information signals raised while setting parameters — with_info_level
code: # Wrap the body of a function that reports, and everything raised inside it # is collected and given together once the call has finished. myConstructor <- function(x, info_level = default_info_level()) {     with_info_level(info_level = info_level, {         signal_info("h", "No `h` provided, using a default.", level = 1)         signal_info("gamma", "Calculating `gamma` from `f0`.")         x     }) } myConstructor(1) #> ℹ No `h` provided, using a default. #> ℹ Calculating `gamma` from `f0`. #> [1] 1  # `info_level = 1` keeps only the report that was marked important. myConstructor(1, info_level = 1) #> No `h` provided, using a default. #> [1] 1  # `info_level = 0` is silence. myConstructor(1, info_level = 0) #> [1] 1

Error messages referred w_max species’ “maximum size” now correctly describe upper size-grid boundary, consistent w_max purely computational parameter. newSingleSpeciesParams(), newTraitParams() newCommunityParams() now document place size-grid boundary maximum size (w_max = w_repro_max): yet set stochastic growth diffusion, individual grows beyond w_repro_max, headroom needed. revisited constructors gain diffusion parameter (#339). print() ArraySpeciesBySize, ArrayTimeBySpecies, ArrayResourceBySize, ArrayTimeByResourceBySize ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize objects (returned getEncounter(), getBiomass(), getResourceMort(), NResource(), getFMort() similar functions) now prints array’s actual values instead per-species min/mean/max summary, truncating large arrays fit console: species shown leading subset, sizes evenly log-spaced sample across full size range, time series representative sample time steps always includes first last, note reporting much omitted. three-dimensional ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize object previewed via final time slice, matching plot()’s existing default class. Use .data.frame() full, untruncated access data. plotYieldGear() now supports log_x, log_y, log arguments, aligning arguments plotYield(). upper boundary condition size-spectrum solvers now holds abundance zero species’ maximum size w_max. Without diffusion automatic results unchanged, predation diffusion switched stops small amount density leaking sizes w_max. See “Numerical Details” vignette.

title: mizer 3.2.0
text: “Getting started” guide now includes self-contained “worked example: Celtic Sea” section takes real ecosystem raw species parameters building, finding steady state, calibrating observed biomasses growth, checking observed yields, setting resilience fishing, projecting fishing scenario whose sustainable-yield curve interpreted — whole mizer workflow one place (#450). first example “Getting started” guide longer prints parameter-default notes newMultispeciesParams(), alarming new users context (#450). Added three new cheatsheets: “Model Setup Calibration” (building model, finding steady state, calibrating observed biomass/yield/growth, projecting), “Fishing” (gears, selectivity functions, catchability, effort), “Changing Model Parameters” (distinction given_species_params(), calculated_species_params() species_params(), changing species parameter updates size-dependent rate versus freezing , gear_params() resource setters differ). analysis--plotting cheatsheet now covers newer plotting functions (plotCDF(), plotSpectra2(), plotSpectraRelative(), plotCDF2(), plot2(), plotRelative(), animate()) ArrayResourceBySize class, corrects interactive-plot advice array objects use plotHover() (ggplotly() method). reference index website now opens “Overview: mizer workflow” section frames whole page five-stage pipeline (create → calibrate → tune dynamics → project → analyse) links key function stage, readers can see sections fit together. reference index website now explains differences related families functions. disambiguates calibrate...()/match...() ...Biomass/...Number calibration functions plot...() variants (...2, ...Relative, ...ObservedVsModel), maps mizer’s mortality-rate names onto standard fisheries notation (M2, F, Z).

Old objects upgraded automatically. newMultispeciesParams(), newTraitParams(), newCommunityParams() newSingleSpeciesParams() gain second_order_w argument (default FALSE, accepting values setter) builds new model scheme already selected. bin_average resource abundance power laws constructed bin-averaged start; construction-time steady-state solve always uses robust upwind flux, chosen flux activated returned model. (#379) bin_average TRUE, every point-sampled power law quadrature feeds finite-volume update replaced exact bin average size bin (bin straddling w_pp_cutoff receiving partial average), sinks, sources capacities consistent bin-integrated encounter convolution (#374): external mortality  (setExtMort()) external diffusion  (setExtDiffusion()); auto-calculated resource intrinsic growth  carrying capacity  (setResource(); user-supplied full vectors left untouched), together matching initial resource abundance  used initial spectrum temporary prey spectra behind default gamma/f0 consumer abundances; predation kernels, now predator- prey-bin averaged (via trapezoid folds), getEncounter(), getPredRate(), getPredMort(), getResourceMort() getDiffusion() become second order change rate functions extra runtime cost. predation-diffusion integral uses dedicated Fourier kernel held new ft_pred_kernel_d slot, carries extra power prey size (,  Jacobian) diffusion integrand needs; first-order scheme equals ft_pred_kernel_e, existing models byte-identical. title: mizer 3.1.0
text: project() gains new time-stepping option method = "tr_bdf2". L-stable, second-order TR-BDF2 scheme retains second-order accuracy method = "predictor_corrector" damping oscillations Crank-Nicolson corrector can show large time steps. See “Numerical Details” vignette. second-order methods ("predictor_corrector" "tr_bdf2") resource now advanced midpoint resource mortality rather start--step value, components (set via setComponent()) now also receive corrector step midpoint rates. resource components integrated second-order accuracy time consumer spectra. "euler" method steady states unchanged.

title: mizer 3.1.0
text: Extension packages can now upgrade data saved model objects independently mizer version. @extensions slot can record, extension, version extension package object conforms (write entries new recordExtension()). needs_upgrading() flags object extension’s recorded version missing older installed package version, validParams() calls extension’s upgrade() method (S3 method utils::upgrade(), registered @exportS3Method utils::upgrade). core mizer upgrade now upgrade.MizerParams() / upgrade.MizerSim() method. See “Upgrading objects across versions extension” section vignette("creating-extension-packages"). getDiet() gains MizerSim method plotDiet() MizerSim now accepts time_range argument, computing diet simulated abundances requested times rather always using initial abundances. MizerSim plotting functions, time_range defaults final saved time step. range spanning several saved time steps given, consumption rates averaged range normalised proportions (rather averaging per-step proportions, normalised independently). (#357) New getFluxGradient() function returns flux divergence  appears transport term discretised size-spectrum equation. bin-boundary fluxes obtained getFlux(), advective-flux scheme stored flux entry second_order_w slot used, largest size class closed boundary condition . Like getFlux(), MizerParams MizerSim methods, returning ArraySpeciesBySize ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize object respectively. getDiffusion() now works custom predation kernel depends predator prey size separately rather ratio. getEncounter(), kernel set (setPredKernel(params, pred_kernel = ...)) diffusion integral evaluated direct summation full predation kernel instead via FFT method, assumes ratio-kernel. (#373) getTrophicLevel() getTrophicLevelBySpecies() now assign resource size-dependent trophic level  instead treating trophic level 0. new w_R (average primary-producer size) beta_R (average resource predator/prey mass ratio) arguments control . Resource functions now return classed objects support convenient print(), summary(), plot() .data.frame() methods consumer rate functions. getResourceMort(), initialNResource(), finalNResource(), resource_rate(), resource_capacity() resource_level() return ArrayResourceBySize object, NResource() returns ArrayTimeByResourceBySize object, can now e.g. plot(getResourceMort(NS_params)) plot(NResource(NS_sim)). summary() MizerSim object now reports fishing effort actually used simulation rather model’s initial_effort. Gears whose effort varied time show mean effort, flagged note giving min-max range. Added new vignette explaining calculation default parameter values (#189).

title: mizer 3.1.0
text: maximum-size species parameters clarified (#325). von Bertalanffy asymptotic size w_inf now required maximum-size parameter used default w_repro_max (previously w_max) w_mat. w_max now purely computational boundary (size grid plot range) defaults 1.5 * w_inf. w_repro_max documented size typical mature individual invests energy reproduction, hard ceiling size. default value external mortality parameter z0 now calculated w_inf rather w_max, purely computational boundary w_max longer influences model parameter. backwards compatibility, w_inf supplied taken w_repro_max w_max, existing models scripts unaffected; however, new models built defaults may differ 3.0.0.

title: mizer 3.1.0
text: Fixed bug project() abundances components (set via setComponent()) advanced per saved time step instead per dt time step. dynamics now integrated time step consumer resource spectra, results longer depend t_save. getGrowthCurves() longer emits cryptic collapsing unique 'x' values warning species’ w_max lies exactly grid point. (#413) getRDI(), getRDD() getFlux() MizerSim object now correctly use simulated time-varying effort instead initial effort. (#370) plotCDF() / plotlyCDF() now plot cumulative value bin’s upper edge w_k + dw_k, following inclusive cumulative-sum convention (sum bin k integral bin’s upper edge). corrects long-standing one-bin location offset applies default second-order schemes; second-order bin-averaging CDF second-order accurate placement well increments. (#383) plotYield() now uses sim2 = NULL instead missing(sim2) detect optional second simulation argument, works correctly .call(). backward-compatible. distanceMaxRelRDI() now returns Inf instead NaN previous RDI zero, projectToSteady() longer mistakes NaN distance convergence.

title: mizer 3.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-06-08 release brings new biological realism, improved numerics, richer interactive analysis experience, composable extension framework. overview see blog post pre-announcing release.

title: mizer 3.0.0
text: McKendrick-von Foerster equation now supports diffusion term, allowing individual variability growth modelled. New getDiffusion() calculates total diffusion rate D(w) (g²/year) species, combining predation-induced diffusion jump-growth equation externally specified diffusion set via setExtDiffusion(). MizerParams MizerSim methods returns ArraySpeciesBySize ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize object respectively, consistent rate-getter functions. external diffusion coefficient held new ext_diffusion slot MizerParams. Use setExtDiffusion() / ext_diffusion() / ext_diffusion<-() set retrieve . new species parameter D_ext (default 0) sets coefficient external diffusion power law; setExtDiffusion() calculates default array species parameters custom array supplied, following pattern setExtEncounter(). MizerParams gains use_predation_diffusion slot (logical, default FALSE). FALSE (default), mizerDiffusion() omits predation-induced diffusion term, preserving behaviour previous mizer versions. Set TRUE via new use_predation_diffusion() accessor enable jump-growth diffusion term. New getFlux() function calculates flux individuals entering size class, combining advective flux somatic growth diffusive flux. power argument, similar plotSpectra(), multiplying flux power weight; power = 1 gives flux biomass. getRequiredRDD() exported. calculates recruitment rate needed maintain given initial abundance, accounting growth diffusion. steadySingleSpecies() correctly preserves steady state project(), including diffusion non-zero. vignette cohort dynamics demonstrates effect diffusion example.

text: project(), projectToSteady() steady() gain method argument choosing consumer density time-stepper. default "euler" preserves existing semi-implicit update, "predictor_corrector" uses new second-order predictor-corrector method. accuracy two methods compared numerical details vignette. MizerSim objects now sim_params slot (named list) records projection parameters — currently method dt — passed project() projectToSteady(). new getSimParams() accessor retrieves list. project() called existing MizerSim object defaults dt method stored sim_params, warning supplied values differ. what: Convenient plot methods for mizer return values
title: mizer 3.0.0
text: New ArraySpeciesBySize S3 class species × size arrays returned many mizer functions. ArraySpeciesBySize object behaves like regular matrix arithmetic subsetting carries human-readable value_name units attribute provides enhanced print(), summary(), plot(), .data.frame() methods. plot() method accepts log_y, wlim, ylim arguments controlling y-axis scale limits. New ArrayTimeBySpecies S3 class time × species arrays returned getBiomass(), getSSB(), getN(), getYield() called MizerSim object. Like ArraySpeciesBySize, carries value_name units attributes provides enhanced print(), summary(), plot(), .data.frame() methods. plot() method accepts log ylim arguments. New ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize S3 class time × species × size arrays. N() accessor MizerSim object now returns ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize object. Many rate-getter functions — getEGrowth(), getEReproAndGrowth(), getPredMort(), getFMort(), getMort(), getFeedingLevel(), getEncounter(), getPredRate(), getRDI(), getRDD() — now also accept MizerSim object return ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize. animate() method allows interactive playback. Subsetting ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize object returns ArraySpeciesBySize object single time selected, ArrayTimeBySpecies object single size selected. New plot2() generic methods comparing two compatible mizer array objects one plot, species group shown colour model linetype. plotSpectra2() helper moved mizerExperimental mizer comparing two abundance spectra. New plotRelative() generic methods plotting symmetric relative difference two compatible mizer array objects. plotSpectraRelative() plotlySpectraRelative() helpers moved mizerExperimental mizer. New plotCDF() plotCDF2() generics plotting cumulative abundance biomass distributions MizerParams MizerSim objects, together plotlyCDF() plotlyCDF2() wrappers. New plotHover() generic methods ArraySpeciesBySize, ArrayTimeBySpecies, ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize, mizer_plot converts mizer plots hover-enabled plotly figures. New addPlot() generic methods adding ArraySpeciesBySize ArrayTimeBySpecies values extra lines existing compatible ggplot. animate() methods produces animated plots showing time evolution simulation. can take aMizerSim ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize argument supports axis range settings (xlim, ylim), timing controls, interpolation options, arguments log_x log_y log control axis log-transformed, total background arguments, consistent plotSpectra(). Plotting functions now consistently expose log_x, log_y log arguments. cases, supplied, log overrides log_x log_y. plotBiomass() plotYield() keep support logical log values backward compatibility. Time-filtering now consistent across time-series plot functions via new tlim parameter (analogous wlim ylim): length-two numeric vector c(start, end) restricts plotted time window. plotYield(), plotYieldGear(), animate() gain parameter first time. plotBiomass() animate.MizerSim() now use tlim place former start_time/end_time time_range parameters respectively; old parameters deprecated removed future release. Size-based plots now accept size_axis = "l" show length cm size axis instead weight grams, using species’ allometric weight-length relationship. Size-based plots size_axis argument now accept llim, length-axis equivalent wlim, filtering limiting plots size_axis = "l".

what: Extracting model state from a simulation
title: mizer 3.0.0
text: shift interpretation MizerParams object just specification model representation state, consisting model parameters current values state variables (abundances). getParams(sim, time_range, geometric_mean = FALSE) now extracts ecosystem state MizerSim object particular time averaged time range. time_range given, state final time step extracted. New finalParams(sim) initialParams(sim) return states initial final times simulation respectively. state extracted simulation, can analysed existing mizer functions. purpose indicator functions getProportionOfLargeFish(), getMeanWeight(), getMeanMaxWeight(), getCommunitySlope() now also accept MizerParams object return single value (named vector getMeanMaxWeight() measure = "") calculated state. Closes #262. setInitialValues() deprecated. Replace setInitialValues(params, sim) finalParams(sim) (getParams(sim, time_range, geometric_mean) averaging time range).

what: New extension mechanism allowing extension chains
title: mizer 3.0.0
text: Many functions now S3 generics methods MizerParams MizerSim objects, users can define subclass methods modify mizer behaviour (#330). New composable extension chain infrastructure: registerExtensions(), getRegisteredExtensions(), coerceToExtensionClass(), clearExtensionChain(), registerExtension(). Extension classes S3 marker classes; MizerSim derives extension chain sim@params@extensions. Extensions provide marker class remain metadata-trigger S3 projection-rate dispatch path. S3 projection hooks added standard mizer rate functions. Extension-aware projections dispatch projectRates(), projectEncounter(), projectFeedingLevel(), projectEReproAndGrowth(), projectERepro(), projectEGrowth(), projectDiffusion(), projectPredRate(), projectPredMort(), projectFMort(), projectMort(), projectRDI(), projectRDD(), projectResourceMort() — models without extensions continue use pre-resolved mizerRates() pipeline directly, per-step overhead. MizerSim accessors getParams(), validSim(), N(), NResource(), finalN(), finalNResource(), idxFinalT(), getTimes(), getEffort(), now registered S3 generics MizerSim methods, making extension-specific methods possible. validParams() also now S3 generic. saveParams() now serialises extension objects plain MizerParams objects preserving extension chain, readParams() restores appropriate extension class. New saveSim() readSim() helpers provide lifecycle MizerSim objects. Extension installation support now integrates pak managing missing outdated extension packages. New vignette Extending mizer documents use setRateFunction(), setComponent(), customFunction(), summarises required function signatures return shapes, gives worked examples custom encounter function added ecosystem component. companion vignette Using extension packages aimed users extension packages, Creating mizer extension package guides extension authors setting new extension package. setRateFunction() now validates registered function calling test inputs checking return value correct dimensions, catching mismatched custom rate functions registration time rather simulation run. Closes #167. setComponent() now accepts optional colour linetype arguments applies via setColours() setLinetypes() added components can styled directly plots. plot() summary() methods MizerParams, MizerSim, mizer array classes now registered S3 methods rather S4 methods, plot() summary() remain plain S3 generics mizer loaded, avoiding interference S4 method dispatch packages.

what: Species parameters for external mortality, encounter and diffusion rates
title: mizer 3.0.0
text: See model description vignette mathematical details. New species parameters z_ext (default 0) d (default n - 1) add optional power-law term external mortality: mu_ext(w) = z0 + z_ext * w^d. z_ext zero (default) behaviour unchanged. Closes #329. New species parameter E_ext (default 0) sets coefficient external encounter rate power law. setExtEncounter() now calculates default external encounter rate E_ext * w^n custom array supplied, matching pattern setMaxIntakeRate(). reset argument also added setExtEncounter() force recalculation species parameters. New species parameter D_ext (default 0) sets coefficient external diffusion rate power law. setExtDiffusion() calculates default array species parameters custom array supplied.

Closes #205. summary() MizerParams MizerSim now displays metadata @metadata slot, including title, description, authors, DOI, URL, mizer version, creation/modification timestamps (set). Closes #294. New str() methods MizerParams MizerSim objects, mizer array classes (ArraySpeciesBySize, ArrayTimeBySpecies, ArrayTimeBySpeciesBySize), showing clean, compact overview structures without dumping large amounts internal data. new steady argument addSpecies() controls whether steady() called adding new species. constantEggRDI() now accounts diffusion across egg-size boundary, including project() uses "predictor-corrector" method. setRateFunction() now validates custom RDI functions diffusion argument receive projection. Growth now forced always non-negative, preventing unphysical shrinkage. warning issued growth stops maturity size. Added info_level argument projectToSteady(), steady(), setParams(), newCommunityParams(), newTraitParams(), matchBiomasses(), matchNumbers(), matchYields() addSpecies()control verbosity information messages, consistent newMultispeciesParams(). (#341) New function psi() returns ArraySpeciesBySize population-level reproductive proportion. age_mat_vB() now exported. New Cheatsheet: Analysis Plotting vignette provides quick reference functions access simulation arrays, compute summaries, calculate indicators, create plots. Closes #176.
